description: Phrasings that may not appear in any generated artifact. Enforced by tests/constraints/constraint-08-no-vulnerability-claims.test.ts over every file the report stage emits. Each rule states why it exists, because a reader who disagrees with a rule should be able to argue with its reason.

disallowed.reason: Conflates the measured precondition with an unmeasured capability. Determining that a server permits a cross-tenant write would require invoking a tool, which constraint 1 forbids.
Constraint 8. The survey observes declarations. It cannot characterise a server's security posture.
Constraint 6. Published output is aggregate. Individual findings go to the affected vendor privately under DISCLOSURE.md.
Conflict-of-interest control 3. The publisher is an interested party, so its product may not appear in the findings. Attribution belongs in the README, not in the numbers.

Section 6 of the protocol. Every figure carries a denominator, an undetermined count, and a confidence interval. A percentage with no denominator cannot be checked. Applied per line: a line may carry percentages only if that same line also carries its denominator or interval — which is also why the percentages inside a rendered confidence interval do not trip it.

required.reason: The distinction between precondition and vulnerability belongs in the opening paragraph, not a footnote. Getting this wrong discredits the work and everything built on top of it.
The limitations section is not optional and is not an appendix.
